title: Data Backup Routine Timeline
placeholder: Click any checkpoint for what it involves and roughly how long it takes. The two amber ones are the only dates anyone has to put in a calendar.

items.label: Confirm sync is on
detail: What it involves
Open the tracking spreadsheet and the consent-form folder, and confirm each one is actually syncing to cloud backup. Not "should be" — look at the sync status.
How long
About ten minutes, once per semester.
Why week 1
Everything after this assumes backups are running. If this step is skipped, the next fifteen weeks of automatic backup are backing up nothing.

items.label: Backup running
detail: What it involves
Nothing. The backup runs on its own.
Why it is on the timeline at all
Because an automatic backup you never look at feels identical to one that stopped in week 2. Marking the quiet weeks is what makes the noisy ones meaningful.

items.label: Mid-semester restore test
detail: What it involves
Restore one real file from the backup and open it. Not check that the backup exists — restore it, and read it.
How long
About twenty minutes.
Why this is the important one

A backup that cannot be restored is not a backup, and it fails silently. Corrupted archives, expired permissions, and a sync that quietly stopped all look exactly like a working backup until the day you need one.
The rule
A backup you have never restored from is a hypothesis, not a backup.

items.label: Backup running
detail: What it involves
Nothing again. Four more quiet weeks.
Worth noticing
Of sixteen weeks, only two need a person. The cadence is cheap precisely because it is mostly automatic.

items.label: Restore test + archive
detail: What it involves
Verify the backups again the same way as week 8, then archive the semester's records according to the retention schedule.
How long
About forty-five minutes, most of it the archiving rather than the test.
Why the two are joined

The end of a semester is the moment the retention clock starts on a lot of records. Doing the archive at the same time as the check means the deletion dates get set while somebody is already looking at the data.

legend.text: Manual checkpoint — put it in the calendar
Two dates a semester is the whole routine
